discovery: Prediction and discovery of flat bands, correlated insulators and superconductivity in magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene, establishing moiré quantum materials

nominees.name: Allan H. MacDonald
nominees.affiliation: University of Texas at Austin, USA

nominees.name: Rafi Bistritzer
nominees.affiliation: Applied Materials, Israel (formerly University of Texas at Austin)

subfield: Condensed matter physics: two-dimensional and moiré quantum materials
motivation: In 2011 Bistritzer and MacDonald predicted that two graphene sheets twisted by a 'magic' angle near 1.1 degrees host nearly flat electronic bands, where interactions dominate over kinetic energy. In 2018 Jarillo-Herrero's group realized this with tear-and-stack fabrication and observed correlated insulating states and unconventional superconductivity tunable by a gate voltage. Together these works created moiré quantum materials, a new platform where twist angle, stacking and electrostatic gating can be used to design strongly correlated phases. Hundreds of groups worldwide have since found correlated Chern insulators, orbital ferromagnetism, Wigner crystals, Mott physics in TMD heterostructures and, most recently, fractional quantum anomalous Hall states at zero magnetic field. Few discoveries in condensed matter have opened such a broad and lasting field so quickly. The combination of a clear theoretical prediction with an elegant, decisive experiment makes this an outstanding Nobel-level achievement.
